title: RecoverySys Online Validation Primary Sources (2026-11-05)
description: Primary authoritative reference packet for physics equations, constants, OpenRocket benchmark route, and measured flight datasets.

sources.organization: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) / National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / United States Air Force (USAF)
sources.title: U.S. Standard Atmosphere, 1976 (NASA-TM-X-74335 / NOAA-S/T 76-1562)
facts: Defines standard troposphere layer from sea level to 11,000 geopotential meters (H = 0 to 11,000 m')
Standard sea level temperature T0 = 288.15 K (15.0 °C)
Standard sea level pressure P0 = 101,325 Pa (1,013.25 hPa)
Standard sea level mass density rho0 = 1.2250 kg/m^3
Standard sea level acceleration of gravity g0 = 9.80665 m/s^2
Troposphere standard temperature lapse rate L = -0.0065 K/m' (-6.5 K/km)
Specific gas constant for dry air R = 287.053072 J/(kg*K), derived from universal gas constant R* = 8314.32 J/(kmol*K) and mean molecular weight M0 = 28.9644 kg/kmol (NASA-TM-X-74335 p. 4 Table 2)
Ratio of specific heats gamma = 1.40 (dimensionless)
Speed of sound equation a = sqrt(gamma * R * T)
Geopotential altitude H related to geometric altitude Z via H = (r0 * Z) / (r0 + Z) where r0 = 6,356,766 m
derivedValues: At 2500 m matched coordinate: T = 288.15 - 0.0065 * 2500 = 271.9 K
assumptions: RecoverySys treats input altitude as geometric coordinate without geopotential correction below 11,000 m (0.039% difference at 2500 m)

conventions.heightReference: NASA-TM-X-74335 tabulates standard properties by geopotential altitude H. At 2500 m, geometric altitude Z = 2500 m corresponds to H = 2499.017 m' (0.039% difference). Benchmark uses matched 2500 m coordinate.
conventions.gasConstantDiscrepancy: NASA 1976 uses R = 287.053072 J/(kg*K); RecoverySys uses R = 287.058 J/(kg*K) (0.0017% difference). Formula exponent in 1976 standard is 5.255876..., while RecoverySys uses 5.2559 (0.00014% difference). Preset tolerance 0.01% accounts for these explicit numeric differences without physical accuracy claims.

sources.reuseConstraints: Public domain work of the United States Government. Official publication approved for public release with unlimited distribution.

sources.organization: U.S. Navy / Naval Weapons Center (NWC) China Lake & Defense Technical Information Center (DTIC)
sources.title: Parachute Recovery Systems Design Manual (NWC TP 6575 / DTIC AD-A247666)
facts: Aerodynamic parachute drag equation: Drag = 0.5 * rho * v^2 * (Cd * S) (Knacke 1992 p. 5-2)
Nominal/constructed canopy area S0 = (pi / 4) * D0^2 based on flat canopy diameter D0 (p. 5-3)
Projected frontal area Sp = (pi / 4) * Dp^2 based on inflated projected diameter Dp (p. 5-3)
Drag area equivalence: (Cd * S) is invariant; CD0 references S0 while CDp references Sp. Typically Dp ~ 0.65 to 0.70 * D0, so CDp ~ 2.0 to 2.2 * CD0
Flat circular solid canopy drag coefficient CD0 ranges between 0.75 and 0.80 based on nominal surface area S0 (p. 5-3)
Terminal descent velocity v_term = sqrt((2 * m * g) / (rho * Cd * S)) (p. 5-5)
Parachute opening shock force Fo = Cx * (Cd * S) * q, where q = 0.5 * rho * v^2 and Cx is opening-force coefficient (p. 5-3, Eq 5.4)
Typical opening-force coefficients Cx: Flat circular ~1.6 to 1.8; Conical ~1.4 to 1.5; Cruciform ~1.1 to 2.2 (Table 5-1)
Shock cord linear elastic energy capacity: Capacity_J = 0.5 * k * (Delta_L_max)^2, where k = F_rated / Delta_L_max (Section 7.3)
derivedValues: 48-inch canopy area from exact inch conversion (0.0254 m/in): D = 1.2192 m, r = 0.6096 m, S0 = pi * 0.6096^2 = 1.16745403 m^2
Secant linear-elastic cord (1500 lbf, 20 ft, 25%, 6 kg, 65 fps): break extension = 1.524 m, stiffness = 4377.95 N/m, peak proxy force = 721.925 lbf, rating margin = 2.078, energy margin = 4.318
assumptions: RecoverySys computeOpeningShockLoad computes force as Cx * 0.5 * rho * v^2 * S without separate Cd; this is a lumped empirical proxy, not a universal conservative upper bound or material certification
Linear elasticity assumes secant modulus up to rupture; real nylon exhibits strain-hardening above ~10% elongation

units.velocity: Feet per second (ft/s) and meters per second (m/s)

conventions.areaAmbiguity: Parachute ratings often omit whether Cd references nominal area S0 or projected area Sp. Using Sp-based Cd (~1.5) with flat diameter D0 overestimates drag area by ~2.2x.
conventions.screeningProxy: Knacke opening shock and snatch calculations are implemented as generic mathematical screening proxies, not structural or material certifications.

sources.reuseConstraints: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited (Statement A). U.S. Navy technical report.

sources.organization: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Glenn Research Center
sources.title: Flight Equations with Drag (Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics)
facts: Closed-form analytical solution for vertical 1-DOF ascent coasting with quadratic drag under constant gravity and density
Coast apogee altitude equation: y_max = (Vt^2 / (2 * g)) * ln(1 + (V0^2 / Vt^2))
Coast time to apogee equation: t_apogee = (Vt / g) * arctan(V0 / Vt)
Analytical terminal velocity Vt = sqrt((2 * m * g) / (Cd * rho * A))
assumptions: Constant air density rho and constant vehicle drag coefficient Cd across the coast trajectory

Excluded from execution against current production API because production integrateAscent models powered ascent with varying density and mass depletion; unpowered coast is not exposed as a public API seam

conventions.coordinateSystem: Vertical 1-DOF (+y upward, gravity downward). Drag always opposes velocity vector.
conventions.status: Excluded from gating; benchmark proposal retained as not-executable-against-current-production-API.

uncapturedMetadata.reason: Public HTML page consulted online at URL; raw HTML bytes not persisted as offline disk artifact. Usage strictly limited to mathematical derivation of closed-form coast equations.

sources.organization: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Glenn Research Center
sources.title: Earth Atmosphere Equation - Metric (Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics)
facts: Confirms 11,000 meter boundary for Earth troposphere and constant -56.46 °C temperature in lower stratosphere (11-25 km)
Educational piecewise curve fits: T = 15.04 - 0.00649*h (°C), p = 101.29 * ((T + 273.1)/288.08)^5.256 (kPa)
Gas law density equation: rho = p / (0.2869 * (T + 273.1)) (kg/m^3)
assumptions: Constants differ from official ISA 1976 (T0=15.04 vs 15.00 °C, P0=101.29 vs 101.325 kPa, exponent 5.256 vs 5.255876). Must not be conflated with official ISA 1976 standards.

conventions.conflict: Educational curve fits are non-standard; production uses standard ISA 1976 formulations.

uncapturedMetadata.reason: Public educational HTML page consulted online at URL; raw HTML bytes not persisted as offline disk artifact. Distinct from official ISA 1976 standard.

sources.organization: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Weather Service (NWS)
sources.title: Information About Wind Barbs
facts: Meteorological wind direction strictly indicates the direction FROM which the wind is blowing
Direction is specified on a 360-degree compass (degrees clockwise from True North, 0° to 360°)
A South wind (180°) blows northward (toward 0° / 360°); a West wind (270°) blows eastward (toward 90°)
Drift direction opposite to wind direction: drift_bearing = (wind_direction + 180°) mod 360°
derivedValues: Under constant 15 mph wind FROM South (180°): wind speed = 15 * 5280 / 3600 = 22.0 fps
For apogee 3000 ft, deploy 500 ft, drogue 60 fps, main 20 fps:
Drogue phase time = (3000 - 500) / 60 = 41.6667 s; drogue drift = 22 * 41.6667 = 916.6667 ft North
Main phase time = 500 / 20 = 25.0 s; main drift = 22 * 25 = 550.0 ft North
Total descent time = 66.6667 s; total drift = 1466.6667 ft North (bearing 0°)
assumptions: Parachute instant wind coupling without horizontal inertia (standard rocketry drift approximation)

units.direction: Degrees (°), 0 to 360 clockwise from True North
units.speed: Miles per hour (mph) and feet per second (ft/s)

conventions.signConvention: Cartesian drift displacement: dx = drift * sin(drift_bearing), dy = drift * cos(drift_bearing). Inverted wind direction is a critical physical falsifier.

uncapturedMetadata.reason: Public educational HTML page consulted online at URL; raw HTML bytes not persisted as offline disk artifact. Usage limited to meteorological wind direction convention.

sources.title: OpenRocket Technical Documentation (v13.05)
facts: OpenRocket 6-DOF simulation framework and extended Barrowman aerodynamic drag model
Runge-Kutta 4th order (RK4) integration with dynamic time-stepping
Parachute model: Parachute.java implements constant drag coefficient (DEFAULT_CD = 0.8) and area getArea() = pi * (diameter / 2)^2
Streamer model: Streamer.java implements aspect-ratio and fabric-density dependent Cd (max 0.40, default 0.60)
Flight event state machine: Launch rod clearance, motor burnout, apogee, recovery device deployment, ground hit
assumptions: CLI headless automation requires virtual framebuffer (Xvfb) or JPype scripting due to SwingStartup headless check in mainline OpenRocket 23.09

conventions.exportFormat: CSV export via CSVExport.java exports time series with explicit SI units. Simulation summaries stored in zipped XML format (.ork).

sources.reuseConstraints: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike (CC BY-SA 3.0). Free software documentation.

sources.organization: OpenRocket Project / ThrustCurve.org / National Association of Rocketry (NAR)
sources.title: OpenRocket 23.09 Motor Thrust Curves Database (RASAero_Motors.eng)
facts: Certified commercial solid rocket motor thrust curves measured and published by NAR Standards & Testing (S&T)
Standard RASP .ENG format: header with designation, diameter (mm), length (mm), delays, propellant mass (kg), total mass (kg), manufacturer
Contains discrete time (s) vs thrust (N) data pairs for piecewise linear interpolation
Covers motors across classes A through M with certified total impulse and burn durations
assumptions: Propellant mass depletes proportionally to delivered impulse (Tsiolkovsky mass depletion)

conventions.interpolation: Piecewise linear interpolation between recorded test points. Total impulse is trapezoidal numerical integral of curve.

sources.reuseConstraints: GNU General Public License v3 / Open source rocketry database.

sources.title: Prometheus High-Power Rocket TeleMetrum Dual-Deploy Flight Telemetry (2022-06-24)
facts: First-party measured dual-deploy rocketry flight recorded at 100 Hz by commercial COTS avionics (Altus Metrum TeleMetrum v6, serial 5115)

Flight envelope recorded: Boost (t=-0.3 to 4.96 s), Coast (t=4.96 to 29.93 s), Drogue deploy at apogee (t=29.93 s, altitude 3,888.7 m AGL), Main deploy (t=157.97 s, altitude 448.9 m AGL), Touchdown (t=237.94 s)
Peak apogee recorded: 3,903.8 m AGL (12,807.6 ft)
Peak speed recorded: 317.9 m/s (1,042.9 ft/s, Mach 0.93)
Observed GPS pad position: 32.9395046° N, -106.9114515° W (Spaceport America, NM)
Observed GPS landing position: 32.9494937° N, -106.9154488° W
derivedValues: Mean drogue descent velocity: 26.9 m/s (88.2 ft/s) over 128.0 s duration (derived from altitude and timestamp intervals)
Mean main descent velocity: 5.61 m/s (18.4 ft/s) over 79.97 s duration
Net ground drift: 1,171.7 m (3,844.1 ft) at bearing 341.4° (NNW)
assumptions: Vehicle dry mass 14.5 kg, drogue diameter 24 in, and main diameter 120 in are unverified assumptions lacking provenance in the supplied CSV header
Local atmospheric conditions (temperature, pressure, surface/aloft winds) at Spaceport America on launch date are not recorded in the CSV
A proposed ±15% acceptance band is an analyst choice, not a source-stated tolerance standard. Flight comparison is blocked pending vehicle and environmental provenance.

conventions.status: BLOCKED from gating. Not treated as matched flight validation.
conventions.sensorUncertainty: CSV header does not record sensor accuracy or calibration records. Barometric readings undergo pyrotechnic pressurization transients at deployment events.

sources.reuseConstraints: RocketPy software is licensed under MIT; third-party telemetry dataset in repository lacks an independent license header and is used for research observation without broad licensing assumption.

sources.organization: Projeto Jupiter (Universidade de São Paulo) / RocketPy Team
sources.title: Juno III Spaceport America Cup 2023 Measured Flight Dataset
facts: First-party measured flight data from Spaceport America Cup 2023 (10k Solid SRAD category, June 23, 2023)
Registered flight card apogee: 3,213 m
COTS barometric altimeter (Missile Works RRC3 Sport) and COTS GNSS logged simultaneously
Real-world recovery failure mode: README.txt explicitly records 'Flight performance: Only the drogue chute was ejected' (main parachute failed to deploy)
Drogue descent continued from apogee (3,116 m) all the way to ground impact
assumptions: Captures pressure pulse transient during ejection charge before stabilizing, but cannot serve as nominal dual-deployment benchmark

conventions.status: BLOCKED. Useful qualitative failure observation; not a matched-input benchmark.
conventions.sensorUncertainty: RRC3 barometric altitude calculated via standard atmosphere formula; sensor subject to transonic aerodynamic effects and ejection gas ingress (~0.2 s).

sources.reuseConstraints: Shared by Juliana Carloni (Projeto Jupiter) with RocketPy team in 2023 for community validation. Dataset permission acknowledged per README.txt.
